doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Early European visits, the Cavern and Georgie Fame
summary: Georgie Fame was the first to do his material and sounded like him.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Let me ask you this. Had you played in Europe before that, or was this your first time in England?
I’d played in Europe before.
When did you first play in Europe?
I don’t know.
In Scandinavia? Early ‘60s probably.
Let’s see. I think I went the first time.
Georgie Fame was the first guy who did my material.
Well, the Beatles were already out, because I remember we went to the Cave, or what was the name...
The Cavern.
The Cavern. And we also...
I played there with...not the Beatles...

We still have those pins from the Cavern. We brought back one for all the kids. But I remember walking... Where was it that Georgia Fame was playing in? We walked in, and he was singing one of your songs and doing exactly... I mean, it really sounded like Mose, a lot like him.
In the BBC documentary, he said that he deliberately was holding his breath to get that tonal quality.
Yeah, he was so close...
I met him. I went to his house one time. He was married to a rich person, who had a house...
It was like an estate, like some sort of stately manor?
Yeah. It was like a long...
Like the aristocracy. Like some sort of landed gentry.
Yeah. He was married to her at that time. Suffolk, I think.
Oh, really?
Yeah. I think it was Suffolk.
